[head=2][color=#535961]Shinohara Heavy Industries[/color][/head]
Shinohara Heavy Industries is a Japanese megacorporation and the premier supplier of heavy equipment in the sector. Where the League fights for ideals and the Mandate for honor, Shinohara fights for the [bold]balance sheet[/bold]. Every operation is a business decision, every soldier an asset, and every loss a line in a quarterly report.
The company runs on strict corporate hierarchy and polished manners. Employees are expected to be disciplined, loyal, and unfailingly professional, and rank in the company is rank in every room. Beneath the courteous surface, Shinohara is ruthless about protecting its profits and its patents.
[head=3][color=#535961]Executive[/color][/head]
- [bold]Sector Manager.[/bold] The senior executive in charge, running Shinohara's presence in the region. - [bold]Assistant Manager.[/bold] The board-level second who supports and speaks for the Manager. - [bold]Human Resources Officer.[/bold] Handles personnel, discipline, and the paperwork of the company.
[head=3][color=#535961]Corporate Security[/color][/head]
- [bold]Head of CorpSec.[/bold] Commander of the company's security department. - [bold]CorpSec Agent.[/bold] The standard corporate security operator who protects assets and staff. - [bold]Corporate Liquidation Agent.[/bold] Elite security brought in for high-value threats and clean-up work.
[head=3][color=#535961]Staff[/color][/head]
- [bold]Salaryman.[/bold] The rank-and-file employee who keeps operations running. - [bold]MedTech Researcher.[/bold] The company's medical and technical specialist.
[head=3][color=#535961]How to address them[/color][/head]
Address is [bold]polite and corporate[/bold]. Superiors are spoken to by their title, such as Manager or Director, and a respectful [color=#535961][bold]Sir[/bold][/color] or [color=#535961][bold]Ma'am[/bold][/color] is always safe. Colleagues may add the honorific [color=#535961][bold]-san[/bold][/color] to a name as a sign of respect.
Rudeness toward a superior is not just impolite, it is a [color=#d9776c]performance issue[/color]. In Shinohara, disrespect and disloyalty are treated as threats to the company itself. See the [color=#e8b04b]Forms of Address[/color] page for more.
